title: Evolvable competency rises rapidly and plateaus at a high level

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolvable competency rises rapidly and plateaus at a high level

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the 1D artificial embryogeny model, when competency is set by an evolvable gene (range 1–500, initialized at 1–15), the best individual's competency rose rapidly and plateaued around 470, higher than the roughly 364 needed for maximum fitness, a level the authors attribute to random drift among equally fit values.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The prevalence of the competency allele rapidly rose, meandering and exploring values up to 485 during evolution (shaded area in Figure 5A) before plateauing at ~470.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “3. Results › 3.4. Evolution Results in a High, Constant Level of Competency”. Scope: In silico 1D artificial embryos with an evolvable competency gene over 1000 generations

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-07: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.87

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The rise and plateau are direct simulation outputs, and the drift explanation can be tested with replicated trajectories and altered tie-breaking. Public methods are adequate for reimplementation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve the competency gene from 1-15 for 1000 generations over many seeds and measure trajectories, stable values, and the minimum competency needed for maximal fitness. Test whether neutral drift among equally fit high values explains the plateau.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Tie-breaking and mutation rules can shift neutral-drift outcomes.

A single trajectory cannot establish a typical plateau.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The evolvable-competency script is public and the decision variable is the competency allele itself. Re-running it tests the rapid rise and high plateau. Exact meander values will differ across seeds, but the claimed plateau near 470 versus the fitness threshold is a stable summary a small team can estimate.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve the competency allele from a low initial range over 1000 generations and record the best individual's competency. A rapid rise that plateaus near 470, above the competency needed for maximum fitness, would confirm the trajectory; a low plateau or continued directional climb would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Stochastic runs will not reproduce the exact path up to 485.

Attributing the excess over the fitness-maximizing value to drift requires showing a fitness plateau, not just a high mean.

fields.label: Hypothesis
fields.value: In a re-implementation of the Shreesha & Levin (2023) evolvable-competency experiment (competency gene in [1, 500] initialised in [1, 15], 1000 generations), the best individual's competency gene rises rapidly and plateaus around 470, above the competency needed to sort its genome.

fields.label: Pass criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered design: 30 repeats x 1000 generations, 100 embryos. 'Best individual' (primary) = the individual with the highest genotypic fitness, first in population order on ties, as in the authors' Exp3 code; secondary = the individual ranked first on phenotypic fitness. 'Needed competency' = number of inversions of the best individual's structural genome (the swaps restricted bubble sort needs to reach fitness 1.0). Using the mean over repeats per generation: pass if all of (R) the mean best-individual competency first reaches 300 by generation 50; (L) its mean over generations 801-1000 is in [440, 500]; (N) that plateau mean exceeds the mean needed competency over generations 801-1000; (S) |mean over 901-1000 minus mean over 801-900| <= 20.

fields.label: Fail criterion
fields.value: Pre-registered: refutes if the plateau mean (generations 801-1000) is < 400, or is not above the mean needed competency, or the mean best-individual competency never reaches 300. Any other failure of R/L/N/S -> mixed. Reported but not entering the verdict: the population maximum competency, the secondary best-individual definition, and the fraction of plateau generations in which >= 10% of the population has phenotypic fitness 1.0 (the tie condition the authors invoke for drift).
